original_question: For the variable-gap middle-interval Cantor-set construction determined by a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} with 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, determine how the answer to the recursive-description problem changes when bilateral symmetry is enforced versus when it is relaxed.
target_in_paper: §4.2, Open Problem OP4 (“Role of symmetry”), read together with OP3 (“Variable-gap deletions”).
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core content of the paper’s target open problem: it uses exactly the OP3 sequence hypothesis 0 < α_n < 1 with 1 - sum_{n=1}^∞ 2^{n-1} α_n >= 0, it asks for a recursive description, and it focuses on the OP4 issue of comparing the symmetric and symmetry-relaxed cases. It also stays in the Cantor-set context rather than drifting to broader unrelated variants.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: the paper studies deterministic Cantor sets on the real line, specifically subsets of [0,1].
The construction should be made stand-alone by specifying the base interval I_0 = [0,1].
At stage n, the deletion is performed from each surviving interval, not just once globally.
The paper’s official wording asks for recursive descriptive formulae for the resulting Cantor set; “answer to the recursive-description problem” is less precise than the paper’s formulation.
The symmetry comparison should be tied explicitly to OP4: the question is how the OP3 recursive description varies when symmetry is enforced or relaxed.
The term “bilateral symmetry” is clarified elsewhere in the same open-problem list, so that wording should be retained only with that context in mind.
On the symmetry-relaxed side, the paper does not specify a single canonical asymmetric deletion rule; it only asks how the OP3 solution changes once symmetry is no longer imposed.

The local benchmark from the paper is the symmetric two-map middle-α family Γ_3(α,2), whose recursive endpoint description is given in Theorem 3.3 and Appendix A; that motivating context is implicit in the draft.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant here; the problem is a real-variable fractal-geometry question, so those data should be treated as inapplicable rather than omitted accidentally.
refined_question: Let I_0 = [0,1], and let (α_n)_{n>=1} be a sequence with 0 < α_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^∞ 2^{n-1} α_n >= 0. In the symmetric variable-gap construction, at stage n remove from each surviving interval its open middle subinterval of length α_n, thereby obtaining a deterministic Cantor subset of [0,1]. Provide recursive descriptive formulae for this Cantor set, and determine how those formulae vary when bilateral symmetry is enforced versus when that symmetry assumption is relaxed.
justification: The draft is aiming at OP4, not a theorem: OP4 asks how the solution to OP3 changes when symmetry is enforced or relaxed. OP3 supplies the exact sequence hypothesis and the variable-gap middle-interval construction. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must restore the ambient interval [0,1], the stagewise deletion rule, and the fact that the desired output is a recursive descriptive formula for the resulting Cantor set. Theorem 3.3 and Appendix A provide the nearest concrete model for what such a recursive description should look like: in the symmetric constant-gap middle-α case Γ_3(α,2), the paper represents the set by recursive endpoint families a_{n,k}(α), b_{n,k}(α), derived from the stagewise middle-interval construction. That is exactly the benchmark against which OP4 asks the variable-gap symmetric/non-symmetric comparison to be understood.
